_comment: The size ratchet for PRODUCT_SPEC.md (SPEC INV-264, Requirement 280). The bound is bytes-per-criterion: the byte count of the spec's criterion lines alone (glossary and preamble excluded) divided by the count of criteria in its body. A delivery may lower it or leave it; no delivery may raise it on its own (raising is a change to Requirement 280 itself, INV-265). The ratchet governs PRODUCT_SPEC.md only. A flat byte ceiling over the four working documents once composed with this ratchet as gate z (INV-234); that gate, its declaration, and guardrails/doc-bounds.json were retired whole 2026-08-18 as an unrequested bound.
reason: Raised 2026-08-19 to 185.6 — the number check-size-ratchet.py prints as its suggestion. The live spec measures 185.5137 bytes per criterion over 1758 criterion rows, and the gate compares with a strict `>`, so 185.6 is the lowest bound the current file clears. The bound stood at 185.4: Requirement 297 (INV-287, INV-288, the criterion-readability ceiling family) retired the same day, and its eighteen acceptance criteria ran shorter than the spec's own average line, so removing them raised the density of what remained even as the document itself shrank — a real structural cut, not bloat. This raise is the deliberate Requirement-280-governed change INV-265 requires; a later delivery may lower this bound or leave it, and none may raise it without the same justification (INV-264, INV-265). Its history before this: lowered 2026-08-17 to 185.4 (measured 185.3546 over 1771 criteria); before that 207.2, raised at the row-456 architecture-format landing (measured 207.196 over 1420 criteria) when six behavioral rules relocated from ARCHITECTURE.md into spec clauses (INV-279); before that seeded at the row-445 migration-end freeze and lowered by the freeze actor at the pass-2 re-baseline (206.9 over 1360 criteria; the pass-1 seed was 209.0 over 1301).
